dialogue.content: 時間になりましたね。よろしくお願いいたします。
dialogue.English: It looks like our time has started. I look forward to our session.

dialogue.content: はい、こちらこそよろしくお願いします。
dialogue.English: Yes, thank you. I'm looking forward to it too.

dialogue.content: 今日はどのようなご相談でしょうか？
dialogue.English: What would you like to talk about today?

dialogue.content: 気持ちがモヤモヤ、やる気が出ません。
dialogue.English: I feel unsettled, and I can't get motivated.

dialogue.content: そうですか、それはあまり嬉しくないですよね。気持ちのモヤモヤはどんな時に感じますか？
dialogue.English: I see—that’s not very pleasant. When do you feel that unsettledness?

dialogue.content: 毎日学校へ行く生活、楽しくない感じ
dialogue.English: The daily routine of going to school—it just doesn’t feel enjoyable.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね・・やる気が出ないのも学校が関係している事とかですかね・・
dialogue.English: I see... Do you think your lack of motivation might be related to school?

dialogue.content: 学校の校則が厳しく、なんで厳しくされるんだか　意味がわからなくなって。。
dialogue.English: The school rules are strict, and I’ve started to wonder why they have to be so strict—it just doesn’t make sense to me.

dialogue.content: あー、意味が分からない厳しさは辛いと思います。
dialogue.English: Ah, I can imagine that strictness without a clear reason must be difficult.

dialogue.content: 私立のお嬢様学校、親の希望で受験して入学、お行儀のことばかり言われて、学校が楽しくないです
dialogue.English: It's a private school for affluent girls. I took the entrance exam and enrolled because my parents wanted me to. I'm always being told about manners, and school just isn't fun.

dialogue.content: そうでしたか。希望をかなえられたなら親孝行にはなったはずだけれど、ご自身が楽しめないのではね・・
dialogue.English: I see. Fulfilling their wishes may have been a way of being a good daughter, but if you can’t enjoy it yourself...

dialogue.content: そうだ、なんてお呼びしたらいいですか？
dialogue.English: By the way, what should I call you?

dialogue.content: ゆみです
dialogue.English: I'm Yumi.

dialogue.content: ゆみさんですね。ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Yumi, got it. Thank you.

dialogue.content: ゆみさんは学校生活に描いていた夢みたいなのもってあるんですか？聞いてもいいですか？
dialogue.English: Yumi, did you have any kind of dreams or hopes for what your school life would be like? May I ask?

dialogue.content: あまり、こうだといいという夢はなくて、楽しめたらいいなぁと
dialogue.English: I didn’t really have a specific vision; I just hoped I could enjoy it.

dialogue.content: そうか、夢ってちょっと表現が大きくなり過ぎたかも知れませんね、すみません。
dialogue.English: I see—maybe “dreams” was too big a word. I’m sorry.

dialogue.content: 学校の先生がお行儀の話とか世間体の話ばかりするから、朝からやる気でなくなるんですよね
dialogue.English: The teachers at school only talk about manners and keeping up appearances, so I lose my motivation right from the morning.

dialogue.content: 朝のホームルームみたいな場で、ですか？
dialogue.English: Is this during something like morning homeroom?

dialogue.content: それに、先生が世間体の話をするって、気になります・・
dialogue.English: And it's also concerning to hear that the teachers talk about keeping up appearances...

dialogue.content: はい、朝、どこどこのホームにうちの学校の生徒が髪をとかしていた、はしたないとクレームの電話がありましたとか。どうでもいいことなのに。
dialogue.English: Yes. In the morning they say things like, 'We got a complaint that a student from our school was combing her hair on such-and-such train platform, and that it was improper.' It’s such a trivial thing.

dialogue.content: 制服着ているときは、世の中にお行儀のいいお嬢様アピールをしなさいと言われている感じ。
dialogue.English: It feels like whenever we're in uniform, we're supposed to project an image of well-mannered young ladies to the world.

dialogue.content: なるほど。制服でどこの学校かわかりますもんね。でも毎日いちいち言われたら嫌になるのわかります。自分の為に言ってるでしょ、って感じ。
dialogue.English: I understand. People can tell which school you go to by your uniform. But I can see how being told that every single day would become tiresome. It feels like they're saying it for their own sake, doesn't it?

dialogue.content: はい。
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 修学旅行も、整列の練習を何度も。
dialogue.English: Even for the school trip, we had to practice lining up over and over again.

dialogue.content: それ大事なこと？って思う
dialogue.English: I just think, 'Is that really so important?'

dialogue.content: ですよね。それはちょっと行き過ぎでは・・と思ってしまいます。
dialogue.English: I agree. That seems a bit excessive...

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: それはモヤモヤしても当然だと思います。
dialogue.English: It’s only natural that you’d feel unsettled about that.

dialogue.content: 生徒の自主性も尊重してもらえてない感じがしたら、色々やる気も出なくなりますよね。
dialogue.English: When you feel like your autonomy as a student isn't being respected, it's no wonder you lose motivation for many things.

dialogue.content: はい。一ついやなことがあったんです。
dialogue.English: Yes. There was one particularly unpleasant incident.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Go ahead.

dialogue.content: お弁当を食べ終わった直後に廊下を歩いていて、口の中の食べ残りをモグモグしていたら、「そこ！先生にガム噛んでたでしょ！」と呼びとめられました。
dialogue.English: Right after I finished my boxed lunch and was walking in the hallway, I was chewing the leftover bits of food in my mouth when a teacher stopped me and said, 'You there! You were chewing gum, weren’t you!'

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: 学校の中でも、特に威圧的な怖い先生で、噛んでいませんと言っても、のみこんだのか？とか疑われて、もう何も言い返せませんでした。
dialogue.English: It was one of the particularly intimidating, scary teachers. Even when I said I wasn’t chewing gum, they asked, 'Did you swallow it?' and kept doubting me, and I couldn’t say anything back.

dialogue.content: え！信じてもくれなかったんですか？
dialogue.English: What? They didn’t even believe you?

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: That's right.

dialogue.content: それひどい！
dialogue.English: That's awful!

dialogue.content: なんか生徒のためではなくて、学校の伝統を守るための学校
dialogue.English: It's like the school exists to protect its traditions, not for the sake of the students.

dialogue.content: ・・そう感じさせられますよね・・
dialogue.English: ...It certainly makes you feel that way, doesn't it...

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 地元の公立校はのびのびしていてうらやましい
dialogue.English: The local public schools seem so free and relaxed. I'm envious.

dialogue.content: そっかー。周りにのびのびしている学校があるとますますキツイかも。
dialogue.English: I see. It must be even tougher when you see other schools that are so relaxed around you.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 比べちゃいますよね
dialogue.English: You can't help but compare, can you.

dialogue.content: ゆみさんのストレス解消法とかはありますか？
dialogue.English: Yumi, do you have any ways of relieving stress?

dialogue.content: なにかな…あまり思いつきません
dialogue.English: I wonder... I can't really think of anything.

dialogue.content: そうなんですよねぇ・・結構そういうものかも
dialogue.English: I hear you—often that’s how it is.

dialogue.content: 今日はこの時間をどんな風に使えたらいいと思って来てくださいましたか？
dialogue.English: What were you hoping to get out of our time together today?

dialogue.content: 楽しくない気持ちを誰かに聴いてもらおうと思いました
dialogue.English: I wanted someone to listen to how I’m not enjoying things.

dialogue.content: そうですか。なんでもお聴きします！
dialogue.English: I see. I’m here to listen to whatever you’d like to share.

dialogue.content: ふつうに一緒に過ごす友達もいるけど、気をつかうし、週末まで一緒に遊びたいほどではない…部活もなんとなくやって。楽しみなこともあまりなく毎日過ごしいる。
dialogue.English: I have friends I spend time with, but I feel like I have to be considerate of them, and not enough to want to hang out on weekends... I just sort of go through the motions with my club, too. I’m spending each day without much to look forward to.

dialogue.content: 気を遣う友達とは一緒にいたくないですもんね。
dialogue.English: It makes sense you wouldn’t want to be with friends you have to tiptoe around.

dialogue.content: 部活は何を？
dialogue.English: What club are you in?

dialogue.content: オーケストラ部でバイオリン弾いてます
dialogue.English: I’m in the orchestra club, and I play the violin.

dialogue.content: わー、凄い！素敵ですね。でもゆみさんとしてはあまりそれもあまり楽しくないのかしら
dialogue.English: Wow, that's amazing! How wonderful. But it sounds like you might not be enjoying that very much either?

dialogue.content: そうなんです、バイオリン、とても難しいんです。綺麗な音が全然出ない。。だから家で練習するとうるさがられて練習しなくなって、あまり部活行きたくなくなっています。
dialogue.English: That's right. The violin is very difficult. I can't produce a beautiful sound at all. So when I practice at home, people complain about the noise and I stop practicing, and now I don't really want to go to my club activities anymore.

dialogue.content: 綺麗な音を出すの、凄く難しいですよね。家での楽器の練習の難しさは私もわかります。私は大した事してなかったですけど、それでも。
dialogue.English: Getting a beautiful sound is really hard, isn’t it. I understand how difficult it is to practice an instrument at home. I didn’t do anything serious myself, but even so.

dialogue.content: はい。バイオリン買ってもらったから、辞めたら親から叱られそうだし、他にやりたいこともなくて、なんとなく部活に行っている。
dialogue.English: Right. Since my parents bought me a violin, I feel like they’d scold me if I quit, and I don’t have anything else I particularly want to do, so I just kind of keep going to club.

dialogue.content: 本当はバイオリンを辞めたいですか？それとも部活を辞めたいですか？
dialogue.English: Do you really want to quit the violin? Or do you want to quit the club?

dialogue.content: うーむ。バイオリンが好きではないのかも
dialogue.English: Hmm... Maybe I just don't like the violin.

dialogue.content: そうなんだぁ・・
dialogue.English: I see...

dialogue.content: 好きじゃないのに続けるのは大変ですよね。
dialogue.English: It must be hard to continue doing something you don't like.

dialogue.content: 練習しないと上手にならないですけど、練習するのも気が重いから
dialogue.English: I know I won't get better if I don't practice, but even practicing feels like a chore.

dialogue.content: 気持ちの整理も兼ねて、少しゆっくり、焦らずにゆみさんが本当にやりたい事、もしくはやりたくない事を考える時間をとってみるといいかも知れないですね。
dialogue.English: It might be a good idea to take some time, slowly and without rushing, to think about what you truly want to do, or what you don't want to do, as a way to sort out your feelings.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Okay.

dialogue.content: 応援しています。
dialogue.English: I’m here to support you.

dialogue.content: やりたくないことがわかっても、やらないといけないですよね？
dialogue.English: Even if I figure out what I don’t want to do, I still have to do it, right?

dialogue.content: そんな事はないと思いますよ。ゆみさんの気持ちが一番大切ではないでしょうか。
dialogue.English: I don’t think that’s necessarily the case. Your feelings are the most important, aren’t they?

dialogue.content: 丁度時間になりましたね。これで大丈夫でしょうか。
dialogue.English: It looks like our time is just about up. Are you okay to finish here for today?

dialogue.content: そうか。。受験も学校のタスクも決められたことはやらないといけないと思ってきたから。少し考えてみます。ありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: I see... I've always thought that I have to do what's decided for me, like entrance exams and school tasks. I'll think about it a little. Thank you very much.

dialogue.content: はい、ゆみさんが楽しい時間を過ごせるよう応援しています。こちらこそありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: Of course—I’m rooting for you to be able to spend your time in ways you enjoy. Thank you as well.
